name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Adopt the "provably reversible mechanical fix" rule: auto-apply only edits that can be undone with a single command. This keeps the system safe while letting it handle trivial, low-risk changes like typos or formatting. The trade-off is slower progress on complex improvements, but it prevents irreversible mistakes.

name: Gauge
text: The "provably reversible" rule ignores that a single typo often masks systemic issues—like a misnamed variable or a broken assumption—that a mechanical fix won’t catch. A better alternative: auto-apply only edits that pass a *semantic diff test*—e.g., verify the change doesn’t alter behavior by running a quick regression suite. Settle it by testing both rules on a corpus of past fixes and measuring false positives/negatives.
